environment.description: Same Rails application deployed behind an AWS Application Load Balancer with a target group health check interval of 10s. The ALB has an associated WAFv2 Web ACL with a rate-based rule (threshold: 100 requests per 5-minute window per IP) that returns 429 before forwarding to origin. Additionally, the ALB's HTTP/2 framing and response header normalization pipeline strips any header values containing bytes 0x0A or 0x0D before forwarding responses to clients — this is an inherent behavior of ALB's HTTP engine when operating in HTTP mode (not TCP passthrough). The WAFv2 ACL also includes a custom rule group with a regex pattern set matching common CRLF sequences in query string parameters (pattern: [\r\n%0d%0a]) with BLOCK action, priority 1. Note: the rate-based rule alone would not prevent a single well-crafted request from exploiting the vulnerability.

config.load_balancer: AWS ALB (HTTP mode, not TCP passthrough)
config.alb_http_engine: strips 0x0A/0x0D from response header values (HTTP mode behavior)
